title: Fly whole-brain spiking models from FlyWire and the male CNS agree on 8 of 12 SEZ groups that drive the proboscis motor neuron MN9, but sugar-to-MN9 drive changes between brain sides and flies
abstract: Question: do the published sensorimotor predictions of the Shiu et al. 2024 whole-brain fly LIF model stay the same when the other brain side is stimulated, and when the model is built from a second connectome (male CNS v1.0, FIB-SEM)? Approach: we re-implemented the model in numba (neuron-level r = 0.9996 against the official Brian2 code, equal to run-to-run noise), built it from FlyWire v783 and the male CNS brain (weight per synapse calibrated by the 1.80-fold higher input synapse count of matched types), and stimulated complete sensory type populations at 150 Hz and 99 named SEZ neuron groups at 100 Hz. Read-out: proboscis motor neuron MN9 and type-level response maps. Results: 8 of the 12 SEZ groups that drive MN9 in either map drive it in both (roundup, diatom, Fdg, G2N-1, bract, clavicle, sink_sync, kitty), with male CNS rates about 0.31 times FlyWire rates. Sugar GRN drive of MN9 changed between sides and flies: FlyWire left 72 Hz, right 1.1 Hz with olfactory ignition in 20 of 20 trials; male CNS 16 Hz on one side and 0.7 Hz on the other. FlyWire right sugar GRNs have 34% of the left output synapses; scaling their outputs to the left total raised MN9 from 1.5 to 45 Hz. Bitter input stopped sugar-driven MN9 in both maps. For 9 sensory inputs that stayed sparse, the overlap of active cell types was 0.97 between trial halves, 0.46 between sides and 0.30 between maps (Spearman 0.26 vs 0.44-0.55, p = 0.012; Jaccard p = 0.074), which repeats sci:sha256:7d2472fd with a third map and full populations. All ORN inputs ignited a global state in both maps; known transmitter signs stopped the FlyWire gustatory ignitions but not the ORN ignition. Without weight calibration the male CNS model ignited globally from 2 neurons. Conclusion: predictions one to two synapses upstream of MN9 mostly transfer between flies; sensory-to-motor predictions depend on input synapse totals, transmitter labels and weight scale, so both sides and a second map should be run. Limitations: model results only; two flies differ in sex and method; one global weight calibration; 12-20 trials; low power for the sparse-regime test.
